papers.title: Dichotomy results for classes of countable graphs
papers.abstract: We study classes of countable graphs where every member does not contain a given finite graph as an induced subgraph -- denoted by $\mathsf{Free}(\mathcal{G})$ for a given finite graph $\mathcal{G}$. Our main results establish a structural dichotomy for such classes: If $\mathcal{G}$ is not an induced subgraph of $\mathcal{P}_4$, then $\mathsf{Free}(\mathcal{G})$ is on top under effective bi-interpretability, implying that the members of $\mathsf{Free}(\mathcal{G})$ exhibit the full range of structural and computational behaviors. In contrast, if $\mathcal{G}$ is an induced subgraph of $\mathcal{P}_4$, then $\mathsf{Free}(\mathcal{G})$ is structurally simple, as witnessed by the fact that every member satisfies the computable embeddability condition. This dichotomy is mirrored in the finite setting when one considers combinatorial and complexity-theoretic properties. Specifically, it is known that $\mathsf{Free}(\mathcal{G})^{fin}$ is complete for graph isomorphism and not a well-quasi-order under embeddability whenever $\mathcal{G}$ is not an induced subgraph of $\mathcal{P}_4$, while in all other cases $\mathsf{Free}(\mathcal{G})^{fin}$ forms a well-quasi-order and the isomorphism problem for $\mathsf{Free}(\mathcal{G})^{fin}$ is solvable in polynomial time.

papers.title: Maximal Order Type and Width of the h-Preorder on Finite Labeled Trees
papers.abstract: We establish tight bounds for the width and maximal order type of the h-preorder on Q-labeled trees in terms of the corresponding invariants of well-quasi-order Q.

papers.title: Ultrafilter characters and local $\pi$-bases
papers.abstract: We completely resolve Question~5.3 of Kania's paper \cite{Kania} and establish a more general realization theorem. We show that for infinite cardinals $\mu\leqslant\nu<\kappa<\lambda$, a space with \[ \pc(X)=\mu,\qquad\pcl(X)=\nu,\qquad \pcc(X)=\kappa,\qquad\pcd(X)=\lambda \] exists if and only if $\kappa\leqslant2^\mu$. The witnesses may be zero-dimensional and Tychonoff spaces, of the least possible cardinality $\lambda$. They may have the least possible number of non-isolated points, or alternatively be crowded. The main ingredient is an exact computation of the centered local $\pi$-character of star filter spaces in terms of ultrafilter character, obtained from a finite selection lemma for filter pushforwards. We also construct a single space with countable $r$-linked local $\pi$-bases for every finite $r$, centered value $\omega_1$, and any prescribed decreasing value greater than $\omega_1$.

papers.title: Spectral Theory and Descriptive Combinatorics for Non-Regular Borel pmp Graphs
papers.abstract: We continue the systematic study initiated in arXiv:2602.05185 of the relationship between the spectral theory and descriptive combinatorics of bounded-degree Borel pmp graphs, particularly in the non-regular setting. We first adapt a classical result of Nikiforov to give a new spectral lower bound on the approximate measurable chromatic number. For certain non-regular graphs, this bound improves on the approximate measurable version of Hoffman's classical bound established in arXiv:2602.05185. Next, we strengthen a characterization in arXiv:2602.05185 of approximate measurable bipartiteness in terms of the spectrum of the adjacency operator by generalizing to the case of non-regular graphs. Finally, we introduce the measurable domination number and adapt several classical results of Lu, Liu, and Tian to give a bound on the spectral gap of the Laplacian operator in terms of the measurable domination number.

papers.title: The strength of the minimum principle in constructive reverse mathematics
papers.abstract: The minimum principle states that every real-valued uniformly continuous function f : X -> R on a compact metric space X attains its minimum. Working in the base system EL0 of constructive reverse mathematics, we show that the minimum principle is equivalent to weak Konig's lemma and to the Cantor intersection theorem (i.e., the contrapositive of the Heine-Borel theorem). Moreover, the above equivalence naturally extends to the equivalence between the corresponding principles with unique existence assumptions, which are then shown to be equivalent to the Fan theorem for detachable bars and the positivity property for a real-valued uniformly continuous function on a compact space. These results sharpen the equivalence among these principles obtained by Ishihara [Math. Log. Q. (1990), 237-240] and Berger and Ishihara [Math. Log. Q. (2005), 360-364] in Bishop's constructive mathematics.

papers.title: Pseudofinite abelian groups and asymptotic classes of finite abelian groups
papers.abstract: This paper studies pseudofinite abelian groups and counting properties of definable sets in finite abelian groups and their ultraproducts. First, we characterize pseudofinite abelian groups in terms of Szmielew invariants and, building on results of Macintyre, extend this analysis to obtain a characterization of pseudofinite $\omega$-stable abelian groups. We then give an alternative proof that the class of finite abelian groups forms a multidimensional exact class, explicitly describing the possible cardinalities of definable sets in classes of finite abelian groups. We also investigate $N$-dimensional asymptotic classes of finite abelian groups and provide a series of examples showing that, despite the exactness result, several natural classes of finite abelian groups fail to be $N$-dimensional asymptotic classes for every $N\geq 1$. Finally, in an appendix, we characterize the SU-rank of pseudofinite abelian groups, building on work of Rogers. In particular, we show that for every pseudofinite abelian group $A$, either $\operatorname{Th}(A,+)$ is superstable of finite SU-rank or it is strictly stable.

papers.title: Forcing and cardinal invariants of universally null sets
papers.abstract: We study universally null sets in forcing extensions and the cardinal invariants of their ideal $\mathcal{UN}$. We prove that the Miller model contains a nonmeager universally null set of cardinality $\aleph_2=\mathfrak{c}$, answering a question of Brendle and Larson. The proof uses preservation of universal nullity by countable support iterations of Miller forcing and shows that the set of Miller reals added during the iteration is universally null. We also prove that every universally null set in the $\mathbb{PT}_{f,g}$ model has cardinality at most $\aleph_1$, and show that there is consistently a forcing destructible universally null set. For the cardinal invariants, we show that $|X|<\operatorname{cof}(\mathcal{UN})$ for every $X\in\mathcal{UN}$, and that $\operatorname{add}(\mathcal{N})=\mathfrak{c}$ implies $\operatorname{cof}(\mathcal{UN})=\mathfrak{d}_{\mathfrak{c}}$. Finally, we prove the consistency of $\operatorname{add}(\mathcal{UN})<\operatorname{cov}(\mathcal{UN}) <\operatorname{non}(\mathcal{UN})<\operatorname{cof}(\mathcal{UN})$.

papers.title: Intuitionistic and Constructive Modal Logics for Classical Modal Logicians
papers.abstract: This paper gives a survey of propositional modal logic in an intuitionistic setting. Mainly intended for readers already familiar with classical modal logic, we discuss why there are two prominent families of such logics, intuitionistic modal logics (IMLs) and constructive modal logics (CMLs), what motivates their study, and how they compare with each other. We then take a look at the logics lying between the CML and IML traditions, and survey various extensions and $\Diamond$/$\Box$-free fragments. We further record several observations which seem to be implicit or absent in the literature; we point out a small defect in the original semantics for $\textbf{CK}$ and prove Lyndon interpolation theorems for $\textbf{CK}$ and $\textbf{WK}$.

papers.title: Vop\v{e}nka's Principle without Choice: Preservation under Symmetric Extensions
papers.abstract: We give a detailed proof that every set-sized symmetric extension of a model of $\mathsf{ZF}+\mathsf{VP}$ again satisfies $\mathsf{ZF}+\mathsf{VP}$, where $\mathsf{VP}$ is formulated for arbitrary set-sized languages. For each standard $n\geq 1$, the same preservation theorem holds for $\mathsf{VP}(\Pi_n)$, with set parameters and arbitrary set-sized languages. We also prove that $\mathsf{ZF}+\mathsf{VP}$ and $\mathsf{ZFC}+\mathsf{VP}$ are equiconsistent, and that $\mathsf{ZF}+\mathsf{VP}$ proves the existence of a proper class of L\"owenheim-Skolem cardinals. Relative to $\operatorname{Con}(\mathsf{ZF}+\mathsf{VP})$, the axiom $\mathsf{DC}$ is independent of $\mathsf{ZF}+\mathsf{VP}+\neg\mathsf{AC}$. The preservation theorem also yields Feferman-L\'evy and full Solovay models satisfying $\mathsf{VP}$. We consider whether every countable model of $\mathsf{ZF}+\mathsf{VP}$ has a class-generic extension satisfying $\mathsf{ZFC}+\mathsf{VP}$.
